text:
ana: quick proposal: create a small client-side compatibility facade ("compat-facade") distributed as our sdk extension. goal: centralize deprecation handling, retry semantics, header propagation, and feature-gate routing so product teams don't have to replicate migration logic.
jon: high-level guarantees? is this just sugar or does it change call semantics?
ana: (typo) ana: sorry. guarantees: minimal surface change for callers. facade will default to pass-through for current behavior. opt-in behaviors: enable header-aware retries, gracefully accept X-Deprecated-* responses, and on config switch route to alternate base_url. no protocol change unless teams opt-in.
priya: love centralizing this. some concerns: SDK churn, version skew across clients, and security (we'd be shipping routing logic into many runtimes).
tom: version skew is real. how do we ensure old client binaries don't ignore new headers? facade helps because we can roll out behavior server-side as well. but if we rely on SDK to implement complex replay logic that's bad. keep it limited to benign, observable features.
nana: jon: typo again, but continuing: propose the facade exposes three primitives: 1) client.wrapRequest(req) -> injects headers (X-Client-Version, X-Facade-V), 2) client.routePolicy(policy) -> local routing override for canaries, 3) client.deprecationHandler(cb) -> local hook for app telemetry.
priya: what about non-JS runtimes? we have mobile, python, go. Are we shipping multi-language libs?
nana: (ana) yes, but start with first-class SDKs (js + python). for others we publish a reference spec (json config + small shim) and a tiny Go/pure mobile helper. aim for parity in feature set but accept phased rollout.
jon: can we keep server-side feature flags so infra can override client routing? e.g., infra wants to route 20% of traffic from old client versions to new endpoint. Facade should support remote-config.
nana: agreed. remote config + sticky state (per-client) so we can do staged rollouts. config should be signed to prevent tampering.
priya: signing is necessary. also we need to be careful about leaking internal endpoints inside shipped clients. any route override must be domain-limited and obfuscated in bundles.
tom: runtime perf: adding another layer in hot paths could matter (token gen clients, embeddings). keep facade overhead < 0.5ms median. implement as in-memory policy check + atomic config swap. no blocking IO on hot path.
nana: good call. implementation note: facade will load config at init and subscribe to a delta stream. config format suggestion: {"v":"1","routes": [{"match":"/v1/chat","target":"https://new-svc.internal","pct":10}], "flags":{...}}. small, typed, versioned.
priya: testing surface: we need integration tests across SDK versions + golden replays. also add metrics: facade.requests, facade.route.override.count, facade.deprecation.hits, facade.latency.overhead_ms.
jon: +1. add a detector: if a client version uses override routing but is still at high error surface for new endpoint, auto rollback on infra side.
tom: ownership? SDK team to own shipping libs, infra to own remote-config and rollouts, product teams to opt-in for their endpoints. need an escalation path.
priya: legal/security note: mobile stores could be long-lived. we must provide server-side fallbacks for at least 6 months after pushing any breaking changes. facade helps but doesn't eliminate the need.
nana: (ana) good call. propose policy: any breaking removal must have 6mo server-side compatibility, minimum instrumentation, and a sunset schedule published. facade will help accelerate clients but not required.
nana: docs plan: 1 paged quickstart + migration checklist + sample configs. also provide a small CLI tool to generate signed configs for infra rollouts.
nana: (again) sorry for all typos in thread.
priya: rollout plan?
nana: propose: alpha (internal SDK + infra config, 2 teams), beta (open to public services, opt-in endpoints), canary (route 1% traffic via config overrides), GA (stable sdk release + docs + required metrics). timeline estimate: alpha 3 weeks, beta 6 weeks, GA 12 weeks.

tom: action items:
- ana: draft RFC + config schema (ETA 3 days)
- jon: design remote-config signing + delta API (ETA 1 week)
- priya: put together security checklist + mobile compatibility constraints (ETA 1 week)
- tom: prototype JS facade thin wrapper and measure overhead (ETA 2 weeks)
infra-bot: auto: created rfc workspace https://rfc.redwood.local/r/compat-facade-1776004321
ana: ok if I assign infra for remote-config infra ownership?
tom: yes, infra owns config infra and signing keys. SDK team owns distribution and release cadence.
priya: no objections. also add required metrics: facade.requests.total, facade.route.override.pct, facade.latency.overhead.p50/p95, facade.config.update.errors.
jon: small UX request: make the deprecation handler pluggable so product can show client-UI banners.
nana: done. we'll include local hook and sample UI snippet in docs.
priya: one more: telemetry retention for client side logs must be adjustable to respect privacy/PII. default to aggregated metrics + opt-in detailed traces.
nana: agreed. default minimal telemetry, opt-in for debug.
nana: thanks all. I'll post RFC + initial schema later today. closing for now. :rocket:
